previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old female with a complex medical history including kidney and pancreas transplants, mechanical mitral valve replacement, systolic heart failure, and end-stage renal disease was transferred for further management after an initial admission for weakness and pneumonia. She presented with chronic epigastric pain, now thought to be related to mesenteric ischemia in the setting of extensive vascular calcifications, and was managed with increased ranitidine, initiation of omeprazole, and lorazepam at bedtime for symptom control. Pneumonia was treated with a full course of levofloxacin and resolved. An elevated troponin was attributed to demand ischemia, with stress testing showing fixed perfusion defects and an ejection fraction of 21%, stable from baseline. Acute on chronic systolic heart failure was managed by restarting torsemide, leading to improved volume status. Her INR fluctuated from subtherapeutic to therapeutic with warfarin adjustment and a brief heparin drip. She remained stable on immunosuppressive therapy and was discharged home with follow-up plans in cardiology, gastroenterology, and nephrology.

microbiology.comments: NEGATIVE FOR LEGIONELLA SEROGROUP 1 ANTIGEN.            (Reference Range-Negative).  Performed by Immunochromogenic assay.  A negative result does not rule out infection due to other L. pneumophila serogroups or other Legionella species. Furthermore, in infected patients the excretion of antigen in urine may vary.

NEGATIVE FOR CMV IgM ANTIBODY BY EIA.  INTERPRETATION:  INFECTION AT UNDETERMINED TIME.  A positive IgG result generally indicates past exposure.  Infection with CMV once contracted remains latent and may reactivate when immunity is compromised.  If current infection is suspected, submit follow-up serum in 2-3 weeks.  Greatly elevated serum protein with IgG levels >2000 mg/dl may cause  interference with CMV IgM results.
